detail: Canadian interprovincial migration (Fox 2016 ARA&GLM); 90 rows, one record per source-destination migration stream. Gravity/Poisson regression on distance and populations with source and destination as crossed geographic indices; the page documents no random-effects grouping and there is one observation per origin-destination cell.

Social-psychology experiment (Moore & Krupat 1971; Fox 2016); 45 subjects, one row each. A 2 (partner.status) x 3 (fcategory) factorial with conformity (out of 40) as outcome; the experimental factors are fixed and no cluster carries repeated observations.

Minneapolis 2015 neighborhood demographics (ACS); 84 rows, one per neighborhood. A neighborhood-level attribute table (level-2 covariates for MplsStops); each neighborhood appears once, so no grouping factor carries repeated observations, and the page documents no model.

Minneapolis 2017 police stop records; 51920 stops clustered in 84 neighborhoods and 5 police precincts (paired with MplsDemo for neighborhood-level predictors). RULE GAP: neighborhood is a strong multilevel grouping candidate with heavy replication, but the help page fits no model and documents no response column (candidates include citationIssued, personSearch, vehicleSearch); excluded for the undocumented response.

U.S. married women's labour-force participation from the PSID (Mroz 1987; Fox 2016); 753 rows, one per woman. Single-level logistic regression of lfp on household covariates; no cluster carries repeated observations.

Wide form of the same O'Brien & Kaiser (1985) repeated-measures data as OBrienKaiserLong: 16 rows (one per subject) with the 15 measurement occasions spread across columns pre.1..fup.5. Derived twin of the long table, which carries the grouping column id; filed under OBrienKaiserLong.

Interlocking directorates among 248 major Canadian firms (Ornstein 1976; Fox 2016); one row per firm. Poisson/overdispersed regression of interlocks on assets, sector and nation (fixed categorical predictors); no cluster carries repeated observations.

Prestige of 102 Canadian occupations (Fox 2016); one row per occupation. Regression of prestige on education, income, women and occupation type; type is a fixed 3-level predictor, no grouping with replication.
Anscombe's quartet (Anscombe 1973); 11 rows, contrived data holding four separate x/y regression datasets in parallel columns. No grouping factor; a wide collection of small bivariate datasets.

Fertility and contraception for 50 developing nations c.1990 (Robey et al. 1992; Fox 2016); one row per nation. Simple regression of tfr on contraceptors; region is a fixed 4-level attribute, no grouping with repeated observations.

Criminal recidivism follow-up of 432 released convicts (Rossi et al. 1980; Allison 1995); survival data in wide form, one row per convict with week/arrest and 52 weekly employment indicators (emp1..emp52). Documented as Cox/discrete-time survival regression; the loaded wide table has no grouping column carrying repeated observations.
2008-09 academic salaries for 397 professors (Fox & Weisberg 2019); one row per professor. Regression of salary on rank, discipline, sex and service; no cluster carries repeated observations.

1994 Canadian Survey of Labour and Income Dynamics, Ontario (Fox 2016); 7425 respondents, one row each. Cross-sectional wage regression; sex and language are fixed predictors, no grouping with replication.

U.S. state education statistics (Moore 1995); 51 rows, one per state plus D.C. Regression across states; region is a fixed 9-level attribute with one observation per state, no repeated-measures grouping.

Survival of 1309 Titanic passengers (Harrell 2001); one row per passenger. Single-level logistic regression of survived on sex, age and passengerClass; passengerClass is a fixed 3-level predictor, no cluster with replication of interest.

Transaction times in branches of an Australian bank (Cunningham & Heathcote 1989; Weisberg 2014); 261 rows. Regression of time on transaction counts t1 and t2 (a multicollinearity example); no grouping factor.

UN national health/welfare/education statistics for 213 places c.2009-2011 (Weisberg 2014); one row per nation. Cross-sectional regression; region and group are fixed attributes, no grouping with repeated observations.

UN social indicators for 207 nations c.1998; one row per nation. Cross-sectional national-indicator table; region is a fixed attribute and the page documents no grouped model; several columns are mixed-type (object dtype).

GSS vocabulary and education, 30351 respondents 1972-2016 (Fox 2016); documented as simple regression of vocabulary on education. year indexes a pooled repeated cross-section rather than a designed cluster, and the page fits no random-effects model.

World Values Survey 1995-1997 for Australia, Norway, Sweden and the USA, 5381 respondents (Fox & Andersen 2006); documented as a single-level proportional-odds/multinomial logit of poverty. country is a fixed 4-level predictor in that analysis, not modelled as a random grouping.

Contrived weight-loss and self-esteem data over three months for three groups (double-multivariate design); 34 rows in wide form with the repeated occasions in columns wl1-wl3 and se1-se3. The loaded table has no grouping factor column carrying repeated observations.

Well switching by 3020 Bangladeshi households (Gelman & Hill 2007); used there as a single-level logistic-regression example of switch on arsenic, distance, education and association. One row per household, no cluster with repeated observations.

Canadian women's labour-force participation, 1977 survey, 263 women (Fox 2016); one row each. Multinomial/proportional-odds logit of partic on husband's income, children and region; region is a fixed predictor, no grouping with replication.

Box & Cox (1964) worsted-yarn experiment; a 3x3x3 factorial in 27 runs, one observation per cell of len x amp x load with cycles-to-failure as response. Single replication per cell, no blocking or grouping factor.
